subject: Architecture
title: The Greek Temple: Birth of Columns
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Greek Temple: Birth of Columns.

hook.text: The Greeks turned wooden posts into marble columns and created architecture's most copied form.

buildup.text: They developed three column styles: plain Doric, scrolled Ionic, and leafy Corinthian.

discovery.text: The Parthenon's columns lean slightly inward. Perfectly straight lines look curved to the eye.

twist.text: Greek temples weren't white. They were painted in bright reds, blues, and golds.

climax.text: The column orders spread across the Roman Empire and are still used on courthouses today.

punchline.text: Every column on a bank or courthouse began in ancient Athens.

quiz.question: Why do the Parthenon's columns lean slightly inward?
options: To counteract the optical illusion of straight lines looking curved
